newsitem.title: ROMANIA: Road traffic "normal" in Romania, ice on Danube.
newsitem.headline: Road traffic "normal" in Romania, ice on Danube.

text.p: Road and rail traffic returned to "normal" in eastern and southern Romania on Thursday after last week's blizzards, and ice brought shipping to a halt on several areas on the Danube, the news agency Rompres said.
"Traffic is normal on all national roads," Rompres said, adding that although all railway tracks had been cleared from snow some trains are still running behind schedule.
Heavy snowfalls and blizzards had disrupted rail, road traffic and shipping in eastern and southern Romania over the past week, with temperatures of minus 25 degrees Celsius.
At least 43 people, mostly homeless, have frozen to death in Bucharest since Christmas.

Rompres said thick ice had halted shipping on the Borcea channel, one of the Danube's three channels. Ice also prevented shipping on the river's Macin channel between kilometres 15 to 20 and 55 to 64, it said.
Flights were grounded at the international airport of Timisoara, near the border with Serbia, and at the local Tirgu Mures and Constanta airports due to fog, Rompres said.
Bucharest international airport was operational, airport sources said.
